items.name: files.upload_init
items.since: Introduced anna-app-runtime v0.5.0 / dispatcher 0.7.0 · current v0.13.0 / dispatcher 0.17.0
items.direction: Bundle (iframe) → Host RPC → APS → R2 presign
items.summary: Phase 1 of a two-phase blob upload. Reserves a per-(user, App) `aps_entries` row (status `pending`), counts it against the user's byte quota, and returns a short-lived **R2 presigned PUT URL** the browser uses to stream the bytes directly to object storage — bypassing your server entirely. Pair every successful PUT with `files.upload_finalize`; orphaned `pending` rows expire after `ttl_seconds` and free the quota automatically.

wire.auth: Handled by the host page — the bundle never sees the token. Transport: `POST /api/v1/anna-apps/runtime/rpc`, `X-Anna-App-Token`, JSON-RPC envelope. See the section overview.

items.signature: anna.files.upload_init(args: {path: string, content_type: string, size: number, ttl_seconds?: number, metadata?: object, tags?: string[], if_match?: string}, opts?: {timeoutMs?: number}) => Promise<{upload_id: string, put_url: string, headers: Record<string,string>, expires_at: string, r2_key: string}>

params.name: path
params.summary: Logical path under the calling App's bucket. Subject to the same `validate_kv_key` rules as `storage.*` keys (≤ 1024 chars total, ≤ 128 per `/`-segment, no leading `/`, no `.` / `..` segments, no control / bidi / zero-width chars).
notes: Re-uploading the same path produces a new row by default; pass `if_match` to enforce optimistic concurrency against an existing entry's `etag`.

params.name: content_type
params.summary: MIME type the browser will set in the PUT `Content-Type` header. Stored alongside the entry and returned by `download_url` / `list` so consumers can render without sniffing.
notes: Must match the PUT exactly — R2 rejects the presigned request if the header differs from the signed value.

params.name: size
params.summary: Declared byte length. Reserved against the user's APS byte quota immediately; over-quota raises `quota_exceeded` *before* a presign URL is issued.
notes: `invalid_arg` if missing or non-coercible to int.
The actual PUT body length is verified on `upload_finalize` via R2 `HEAD`; mismatch raises `precondition_failed` and the row stays `pending`.

params.name: ttl_seconds
params.summary: Presign URL lifetime AND the `pending` row's reclamation window. Orphaned rows (never finalized) are reaped after this many seconds and their quota reservation is released.

params.name: metadata
params.summary: Free-form JSON metadata stored on the row. Round-trips on `list`. No size limit beyond the row's total JSON budget.

params.name: tags
params.summary: Sortable / filterable tags. Round-trips on `list`. Useful for cheap server-side categorisation without a separate index.

params.name: if_match
params.summary: Optimistic-concurrency guard against an *existing* entry at the same path. Pass the prior `etag` you read via `download_url` / `list`; mismatch raises `precondition_failed`.

returns.summary: Stable id of the `pending` row. Currently equals the APS entry UUID; treat as opaque.
Single-use R2 presigned PUT URL. Browser issues a direct `fetch(put_url, {method:'PUT', headers, body})` — no proxy through nexus.
Headers the browser MUST send with the PUT to match the signature (typically `Content-Type` and any object-lock / encryption headers R2 baked into the signature).
Absolute deadline for the PUT and the pending-row reclamation.
Internal R2 object key chosen by the service (typically `app/<app_id>/<user_uuid>/<path>`). Opaque; not used by the bundle.

errors.summary: Missing / wrong-typed `path` / `content_type` / `size`.
Path fails `validate_kv_key` (segment length, illegal chars, leading `/`, etc.).

`files.upload_init` is not listed in `manifest.ui.host_api.files` — that list is the ONLY ACL gate (`host_api_allows`). `manifest.permissions[]` is display/audit metadata and is never consulted by the dispatcher, and the default app-scoped files bucket needs no `host_capabilities` entry.
Reserving `size` would push the user past `aps_byte_quota` or `aps_entry_quota`. No presign URL issued.
`if_match` did not match the existing entry's `etag`.
`size` exceeds the per-object hard cap (`APS_OBJECT_MAX_BYTES`).
R2 presign call failed or DB write failed.

limitations: Apps cannot stream — body must be sent in a single PUT.
Presigned URL is single-use; refreshing requires a fresh `upload_init` call (and re-reserves quota).
`pending` rows reserve quota until `ttl_seconds` elapses; aggressive UI retries can transiently exhaust quota — surface `quota_exceeded` as a retry-after-delay error.

Availability: the iframe-facing `anna.files.*` surface is served by APS handlers that are only installed when the APS backend is wired. The local-dev CLI harness (`anna-app dev`) returns `not_implemented` for `files.*` unless run with APS forwarding — in that mode apps usually reach object storage indirectly through an Executa's `aps.files` capability instead.

Authoring caveat: the current `@anna-ai/app-schema` does not yet expose a `files` key under `ui.host_api`, so `anna-app validate` rejects manifests that declare `ui.host_api.files` directly. The Python runtime accepts it, but until the schema catches up most apps use `ui.host_api.tools` plus an Executa that performs the APS files reverse-RPC.

items.name: files.upload_finalize
items.since: Introduced anna-app-runtime v0.5.0 / dispatcher 0.7.0 · current v0.13.0 / dispatcher 0.17.0
items.direction: Bundle (iframe) → Host RPC → APS (R2 HEAD verify + row flip)
items.summary: Phase 2 of the upload. Verifies the PUT actually landed in R2 (`HEAD` for byte length / etag), flips the `pending` row to `active`, commits the quota reservation, and returns the canonical `etag` / `generation` you'll use for subsequent `if_match` writes.
items.signature: anna.files.upload_finalize(args: {path: string, etag?: string, size?: number, size_bytes?: number, metadata?: object}, opts?: {timeoutMs?: number}) => Promise<{path: string, etag: string, generation: number, size_bytes: number}>

params.name: path
params.summary: Same logical path passed to `upload_init`. The service looks up the matching `pending` row by `(user, app, path)`.

params.name: etag
params.summary: R2-returned ETag from the PUT response. When provided, the service verifies it matches R2's `HEAD` reply; mismatch raises `precondition_failed`.

params.name: size
params.summary: Alias for `size_bytes` (SDK accepts either). Cross-checked against the R2 `HEAD` content-length.

params.name: size_bytes
params.summary: Declared byte length. Cross-checked against R2 `HEAD`.

params.name: metadata
params.summary: Optional metadata replacement; merges over what was set in `upload_init`.

returns.summary: Canonical path (echoes input).
Stable APS etag (`W/"<gen>-<digest>"`) — feed into later `files.delete` / `files.upload_init` as `if_match`.
Monotonic write counter for the row.
Authoritative byte length per R2 `HEAD`.

errors.summary: Missing `path`.
No `pending` row exists at `(user, app, path)` — either never called `upload_init` or it was already finalized / reaped.
R2 `HEAD` returned a different etag / size than the client supplied (PUT body did not match the signed declaration).
R2 `HEAD` returned 404 — bytes never arrived (PUT failed / abandoned).
Same ACL gate as `upload_init`.
R2 HEAD or DB commit failed.

limitations: Must be called after the PUT succeeds; calling without a successful PUT raises `pending_upload`.
Service identifies the row by `path`; you cannot rename mid-flight — the path passed here must match `upload_init`.
The `upload_id` returned by `upload_init` is NOT consumed here today (lookup is by `(user, app, path)`).

items.name: files.download_url
items.since: Introduced anna-app-runtime v0.5.0 / dispatcher 0.7.0 · current v0.13.0 / dispatcher 0.17.0
items.direction: Bundle (iframe) → Host RPC → APS → R2 presign GET
items.summary: Mint a short-lived R2 presigned GET URL for an `active` entry. Use this in `` / `
items.signature: anna.files.download_url(args: {path: string, ttl_seconds?: number, ttl?: number, disposition?: string}, opts?: {timeoutMs?: number}) => Promise<{get_url: string, expires_at: string, etag: string, size_bytes: number, content_type: string}>

params.name: path
params.summary: Logical path of the existing entry.

params.name: ttl_seconds
params.summary: URL lifetime in seconds. Clamped by `APS_PRESIGN_GET_TTL_MAX_S` server-side.

params.name: ttl
params.summary: Backward-compatible alias for `ttl_seconds`.

params.name: disposition
params.summary: `Content-Disposition` value to bake into the signature, e.g. `attachment; filename="report.pdf"` to force a download dialog instead of inline render.

returns.summary: Presigned GET URL. Stream-safe; embed in `` / `
Absolute deadline; after this the URL returns 403.
Current entry etag (use as `if_match` for subsequent `files.delete`).
Authoritative byte length.
Stored MIME type — handy for `Accept`-based UI branching.

errors.summary: Missing `path`.
No `active` row at `(user, app, path)` (never finalized / soft-deleted / TTL-expired).

`files.download_url` is not listed in `manifest.ui.host_api.files` — that list is the ONLY ACL gate (`host_api_allows`). `manifest.permissions[]` is display/audit metadata and is never consulted by the dispatcher, and the default app-scoped files bucket needs no `host_capabilities` entry.

limitations: URL is single-resource; can't be used for range scans across the bucket.
Browser caches honour the presigned URL's host headers, not the entry etag — refresh by minting a new URL when content changes.
Cross-origin isolation gotcha: if your iframe is in COEP `require-corp` mode, R2 GETs need a `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy` header — see the `iframe-coep-blocks-cross-origin-images` note.

Field name: the presigned URL is returned as `get_url` (NOT `url`). This differs from `image.generate` / `image.edit`, whose results use `images[].url`. The runtime SDK (`anna.files.download_url`) is a thin passthrough and returns `get_url` verbatim — do not expect a `url` alias.

items.name: files.download
items.kind: Host API method · iframe surface · host-mediated
items.direction: Bundle (iframe) → Host RPC → APS → R2 presign GET → host page triggers top-level browser save
items.summary: Host-mediated download for user-facing Save buttons. Same presign as `download_url`, but the `Content-Disposition` is ALWAYS forced to `attachment` and the presigned URL is consumed by the HOST PAGE, not your bundle: `anna-app-host-bridge.js` clicks a transient top-level `<a>` so the browser save dialog opens, then strips `get_url` before the result reaches the iframe. Use this instead of `download_url` + `<a download>` when the goal is saving a file — it works regardless of iframe sandbox tokens and the short-lived bearer URL never enters app-controlled DOM.
items.signature: anna.files.download(args: {path: string, filename?: string, ttl_seconds?: number, scope?: string, owner?: string}, opts?: {timeoutMs?: number}) => Promise<{ok: true, filename: string, expires_at: string, etag: string, size_bytes: number, content_type: string}>

params.name: path
params.summary: Logical path of the existing `active` entry.

params.name: filename
params.summary: Save-as filename shown in the browser dialog. Defaults to the last `path` segment. Baked into the presigned `Content-Disposition: attachment` header (ASCII fallback + RFC 5987 UTF-8 form, so non-ASCII names survive).

params.name: ttl_seconds
params.summary: Presign lifetime. The host consumes the URL immediately, so the default is almost always fine.

params.name: scope
params.summary: Same semantics as `files.download_url` / `files.list` — cross-app reads need `aps.scope.app.read`.

params.name: owner
params.summary: Owner app slug when reading another app's scope.

returns.summary: The host page accepted and triggered the save. NOTE: the iframe-visible result contains NO `get_url` — it is stripped by the host bridge by design.
Effective save-as filename (explicit arg or derived from `path`).
Presign deadline (informational; the host already consumed the URL).
Current entry etag.
Authoritative byte length.
Stored MIME type.

errors.summary: Missing `path`, or non-string `filename`.
No `active` row at `(user, app, path)`.
`files.download` (or `"*"`) is not listed in `manifest.ui.host_api.files`.

limitations: Direct in-iframe downloads (Blob URLs, `<a download>`) additionally require the iframe sandbox `allow-downloads` token — present on hosts ≥ 1.1.0-beta.97. `files.download` works on those hosts without relying on the token.
The download is triggered by a programmatic top-level anchor click; browsers may coalesce/deny rapid repeated downloads without fresh user gestures — call it from a click handler.
Only APS-stored entries are downloadable — this method never accepts raw external URLs (no open-redirect surface).

items.name: files.list
items.since: Introduced anna-app-runtime v0.5.0 / dispatcher 0.7.0 · current v0.13.0 / dispatcher 0.17.0
items.summary: Page through the calling App's file entries under an optional `prefix`. Returns metadata only — no bytes, no presigned URLs. Cursor-based; cursors are opaque and not stable across deploys.
items.signature: anna.files.list(args: {prefix?: string, cursor?: string, limit?: number}, opts?: {timeoutMs?: number}) => Promise<{items: Array<{path: string, etag: string, size_bytes: number, content_type: string, metadata: object|null, tags: string[]|null, updated_at: string|null}>, next_cursor: string|null}>

params.name: prefix
params.summary: Match entries whose `path` starts with this string. Empty / omitted lists the whole bucket.

params.name: cursor
params.summary: Opaque pagination cursor from a prior call's `next_cursor`.

params.name: limit
params.summary: Max rows per page. Service clamps to `APS_LIST_LIMIT_MAX` (typically 1000).

returns.summary: Row metadata only. `value` is never included (use `download_url` to stream bytes).
Logical path under the App bucket.
Use as `if_match` for `files.delete`.
Authoritative byte length.
Stored MIME type.
Whatever was passed at upload time.
Whatever was passed at upload time.
Last write timestamp (UTC).
`null` when the last page is reached.

errors.summary: `limit` not coercible to int.

`files.list` is not listed in `manifest.ui.host_api.files` — that list is the ONLY ACL gate (`host_api_allows`). `manifest.permissions[]` is display/audit metadata and is never consulted by the dispatcher, and the default app-scoped files bucket needs no `host_capabilities` entry.

limitations: Soft-deleted and `pending` rows are excluded.
No sort options — results are returned in the service's deterministic order (typically `path` ascending).
Cursor is opaque and tied to a specific deploy / query plan; do NOT persist across reloads.

items.name: files.delete
items.since: Introduced anna-app-runtime v0.5.0 / dispatcher 0.7.0 · current v0.13.0 / dispatcher 0.17.0
items.direction: Bundle (iframe) → Host RPC → APS (Postgres soft-delete; R2 reaped async)
items.summary: Soft-delete an entry. The row is marked `deleted`, quota bytes are reclaimed immediately, and the underlying R2 object is hard-deleted asynchronously by the APS reaper. Supports `if_match` for safe concurrent-write scenarios.
items.signature: anna.files.delete(args: {path: string, if_match?: string}, opts?: {timeoutMs?: number}) => Promise<{deleted: true}>

params.name: path
params.summary: Logical path of the entry to delete.

params.name: if_match
params.summary: Optimistic-concurrency guard. Pass the etag you last observed; mismatch raises `precondition_failed` so a concurrent re-upload isn't silently clobbered.

returns.summary: Always `true` on success. The service never returns `false` — failures raise instead.

errors.summary: Missing `path`.
No active row at `(user, app, path)` — already deleted / never existed / TTL-expired.
`if_match` did not match the current etag (someone else wrote first).

`files.delete` is not listed in `manifest.ui.host_api.files` — that list is the ONLY ACL gate (`host_api_allows`). `manifest.permissions[]` is display/audit metadata and is never consulted by the dispatcher, and the default app-scoped files bucket needs no `host_capabilities` entry.

limitations: Soft-delete only from the App's perspective — the row stays in `aps_entries` until the reaper hard-deletes it.
Cannot un-delete from this API; the soft-deleted row is opaque to the iframe.
Pre-signed GET URLs minted before the delete may still resolve until R2 reaper runs (typically minutes).
